issues.description: Resolver.resolve() postcondition silently weakened: returned requirements may no longer be `prepared`.
issues.detail: The resolver previously guaranteed every returned requirement had prepared=True and needs_more_preparation=False. The patch deletes that block without restating the contract, pushing the obligation onto every caller. Any consumer that doesn't call prepare_linked_requirements_more (third-party tools, future commands, extensions) gets a silently half-prepared state. Restore the invariant, document the new postcondition, or assert it.

issues.description: set_dist/get_dist cache can return stale metadata-only dist after full preparation, with no documented precedence.
issues.detail: get_dist() now prefers self._distribution over metadata_directory and local_file_path. A metadata-only BaseDistribution cached by _fetch_metadata_only will shadow a later fully-prepared wheel forever, since nothing invalidates _distribution on full prep. Callers can't tell whether they hold metadata-only or installable. Invalidate on full prepare, split accessors, or document the precedence invariant.

issues.description: download_info backfill inside _fetch_metadata_only entangles fetch with reporting and rests on unstated preconditions.
issues.detail: When metadata_dist is non-None, download_info is set via direct_url_from_link(req.link, req.source_dir) guarded only by `if None`. In dry-run, source_dir may be unset and there is no hash, so pip lock / --report output for VCS or non-PyPI links may be silently malformed. The precondition on source_dir is undocumented and untested.

issues.description: prepare_linked_requirements_more call duplicated across three commands instead of a single shared finalize step.
issues.detail: download.py, install.py, and wheel.py each independently call preparer.prepare_linked_requirements_more on the resolved set. That's the same incantation in three places — exactly what the resolver used to own. A fourth command (lock, the very feature this PR enables) will forget it. Extract a helper or restore it to the resolver behind a dry_run flag.

issues.description: No test proves the headline behaviour: --dry-run no longer downloads full wheels.
issues.detail: The news entry promises that dry-run avoids wheel downloads when PEP 658 metadata exists, but the diff contains no test that fails on the old behaviour and passes on the new. A small integration test with a mock index that errors on wheel GET would pin the property. Without it, a future refactor silently reintroduces the regression.

issues.description: set_dist introduced with no specification, invariants, or validation.
issues.detail: set_dist is a one-line attribute assignment with no docstring, no idempotency contract, and no constraint on when it may be called. For a mutable cache touched by resolver, preparer, and installer, the spec is the contract. Either give it a real invariant (settable once, must match req.name, cleared on full prep) or drop the method and document the attribute.

synthesis.summary: The panel unanimously supports the intent — moving eager preparation out of the resolver so --dry-run and pip lock avoid full wheel downloads — but rejects the execution as under-specified. The resolver's postcondition that requirements are fully prepared is silently deleted and scattered into three command-site copies, with no documented contract for callers. The new set_dist/get_dist cache has no invalidation story when a real wheel later lands, risking stale metadata-only dists shadowing the installable one. The download_info backfill inside _fetch_metadata_only entangles fetch with reporting and rests on an unstated precondition about source_dir. Ship-blocking: restore or restate the resolver invariant, define cache precedence/invalidation, and add a test proving dry-run skips the download.
